rachel: quick heads-up  running into a stall when cancelling the streaming client in our Python sample. consumer never exits; socket lingers until timeout. mypy also flags the wrapper as not an AsyncIterator.

sam: can you paste the wrapper you used? sounds like the usual __aiter__/__anext__ typing gotcha.

rachel: tiny repro:
```py
class SdkWrapper:
    async def __aiter__(self):
        return self

    async def __anext__(self) -> Optional[str]:
        chunk = await self.upstream.__anext__()
        if not chunk:
            return None
        return chunk.decode()
```

rachel: mypy says "error: SdkWrapper is not AsyncIterator[str]" and at runtime None is treated as a value so loops never terminate.

jin: two quick fixes: 1) __aiter__ must be synchronous: def __aiter__(self): return self. 2) never return None from __anext__ to signal EOF  raise StopAsyncIteration instead. 3) add aclose()/__aexit__ that propagates asyncio.CancelledError and calls upstream.aclose().

sam: also add a small pytest-asyncio test that cancels the consumer Task and asserts upstream.aclose was called. that'll catch regressions.

rachel: thanks  updating our example in examples/streaming/sdk_wrapper.py and will open a PR with the test and a short doc blurb.

dev-bot: dev-bot created issue REDWOOD-STREAM-5110: "stream wrapper returns None from __anext__ causing hang and typing mismatch" assigned to rachel. :robot_face:

sam: ping me on the PR for a quick typing/async review. :thumbsup:
